subject: biology
title: Molecular Biology Adventure 2: Proteins — primary to quaternary
welcome_lead: Today you'll fold a polypeptide through four levels of structure.
meta_desc: Biology — protein structure, primary to quaternary, denaturation, enzyme function.
final_note: You learned proteins have 4 levels (1° sequence, 2° α-helix/β-sheet, 3° tertiary fold, 4° subunits), and shape determines function.

concepts.def: Amino acid sequence from N to C terminus
Loss of 3D shape from heat or pH
Covalent C-N bond between amino acids

walkthroughs.body_html:
Twenty amino acids share a backbone: NH₂-CαH(R)-COOH. The R-group makes them differ.

Condensation between -COOH and -NH₂ forms a peptide bond, releasing H₂O.

Primary structure is just the sequence — but it dictates everything else.

Secondary — backbone H-bonds form α-helices and β-pleated sheets (Pauling, 1951).

Tertiary — R-groups interact:
- Disulfide bridges (Cys-Cys)
- Ionic bonds
- Hydrogen bonds
- Hydrophobic interactions

Quaternary — 2+ subunits, e.g. haemoglobin (2α + 2β + 4 haem).

Enzymes are globular proteins with an active site complementary to substrate (induced fit, Koshland 1958).

High temperature or extreme pH breaks H-bonds and ionic bonds → denaturation — irreversible loss of function.

Prion diseases (e.g. CJD) show misfolded proteins can be infectious — a paradigm shift (Prusiner, Nobel 1997).

mcqs.q: Which bond forms between two amino acids?
options: Glycosidic
Peptide
Phosphodiester
Ester

mcqs.q: Haemoglobin has 4 subunits — this is which level?
options: Primary
Secondary
Tertiary
Quaternary

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Antibodies bind to any antigen they meet first.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2 in humans.
Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.

mcqs.q: What does it mean for an allele to be 'dominant'?
options: Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
A dominant allele is the most common allele in a population.
It is expressed in the phenotype when at least one copy is present (in a heterozygote).

mcqs.q: What makes the antigen-binding site of an antibody specific to one antigen?
options: A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.
All antibodies have the same binding site; specificity comes from where they go in the body.
Antibodies bind to any antigen they meet first.
The variable region — its amino acid sequence (and thus shape) differs between antibodies, complementing a specific antigen.

options: Multiple polypeptide subunits
Covalent C-N bond between amino acids
3D fold from R-group interactions
α-helix and β-pleated sheet (H-bonds)

Amino acid sequence from N to C terminus
Covalent C-N bond between amino acids
